title: Pardons John Richard Bubala
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to John Richard Bubala as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department’s clemency list records that Trump pardoned John Richard Bubala on July 29, 2019. It identifies a 1991 Southern District of Indiana conviction for conversion of government property and a sentence of two years’ probation, including four months of community confinement and two months of home confinement. The list confirms the pardon but gives no reason for it.
description_long: The Justice Department’s official clemency list records John Richard Bubala among the people President Donald Trump pardoned on July 29, 2019. The same listing identifies a Southern District of Indiana conviction dated April 5, 1991, for conversion of government property. It says Bubala received two years’ probation, conditioned on four months of community confinement and two months of home confinement. The entry therefore provides a basic chronology: the conviction and sentence preceded the pardon by more than 28 years. The list confirms that the action was a pardon; it does not describe the underlying conduct, say whether the sentence had already been completed, or give the administration’s reason for granting clemency. This account stays within those listed facts. It does not infer that the pardon was connected to a political relationship or that the conviction itself establishes wrongdoing by the person who granted the pardon.

title: Pardons Amy Ralston Povah
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Amy Ralston Povah as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department lists Amy Ralston Povah as pardoned by Trump on January 13, 2021. It records a 1992 Western District of Texas sentence of 292 months in prison, five years of supervised release, and a $10,000 fine for conspiracies involving controlled-substance distribution and importation and money laundering. The clemency list confirms the grant but gives no rationale.
description_long: The Justice Department’s official clemency list records Amy Ralston Povah among the people President Donald Trump pardoned on January 13, 2021. It identifies a Western District of Texas sentence imposed on February 27, 1992: 292 months in prison, five years of supervised release, and a $10,000 fine. The listed offenses were conspiracy to distribute a controlled substance, conspiracy to import a controlled substance, and money laundering. The entry places the pardon nearly 29 years after the sentence and provides a concise record of the case history behind the clemency action. It does not describe the underlying conduct, say how much of the sentence Povah served, or explain why the administration granted the pardon. The official list establishes the recipient, date, offenses, and sentence; it does not support claims about political influence or the reasons for the decision. A fuller account of those points would require the clemency record or case-specific reporting.
